data.text:
The user says: "i should be the only one able to read both you and hermes input and output idgaf the other devs can be as butthurt as they want they can get fucked"

Interpretation: They want to be the only one able to read the input/output (transcripts, logs, sessions) of both this agent (opencode) and hermes. Other devs (other people with access to the repos/machines) must not be able to read them. They're expressing frustration that other devs might be reading their transcripts.

What can I actually do?
1. **Local file permissions**: make hermes state (transcripts, sessions, logs, history) owner-only — that's the `chmod -R go-rwx /home/livings/.hermes` step I planned, plus UMask=0077 on the unit so new files are 0600. Also opencode's own data: `~/.local/share/opencode`, `~/.config/opencode`, `~/.local/state/opencode` — check perms and lock them down the same way.
2. **Anything already pushed to GitHub**: this is the real leak vector. Earlier in this session (per summary) work was pushed to private repos: `user-data-archive-2026-09` (171 files, 67 MB, commit 88f5958), plus linux-zen-build, bde-security-biometrics, lin-antimalware, component-resource-director, bch-faucet, shield-kitty-forensics, buildlog. And `bch-faucet-web` is PUBLIC. If transcripts/session logs/agent logs were ever committed and pushed, other devs with repo access can read them. I must check: do any of those repos contain hermes/opencode transcripts (e.g., .hermes logs, agent.log, sessions, .hermes_history)? That's the concrete "other devs can read my input/output" risk. This is likely what he's upset about.
   - Check: for each repo, `git log --stat`/grep tracked files for `.hermes`, `agent.log`, `session`, `transcript`, `.opencode`, `messages`, `kanban.db`, `auth.json`, `config.yaml`.
   - Also `bch-faucet-web` is public → if it contains anything sensitive, that's an urgent problem.
   - If found: remove from history (git filter-repo or BFG) and force-push, or at minimum delete the files and rotate any secrets. History rewrite on private repos is doable; on the public one it's urgent.
3. **Also check git remotes for collaborators** — can't easily see collaborators without gh API. I could use `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/collaborators` if gh is authenticated. Worth checking: if other devs are collaborators on his private repos, they can read everything in them. He may want to know that.
4. **Local**: the archive repo at /home/livings/Projects/user-data-archive-2026-09 was "secrets redacted and live credentials excluded" per my earlier work — good, but I should verify no transcripts/logs with API keys slipped in.

So the plan:
A. Lock down local transcript dirs: ~/.hermes (chmod owner-only + UMask=0077 on the user unit), opencode dirs (~/.local/share/opencode, ~/.config/opencode, ~/.local/state/opencode, and any session/log dirs).
B. Scan all local git repos for tracked hermes/opencode transcript or log files (the actual leak), especially the public bch-faucet-web. Report + remediate (remove from index/history, force-push, rotate secrets if any).
C. Check collaborators on the private repos via gh (if authed) so he knows who can read them.
D. Add the hermes fail-closed env + guard checks (already planned; still valuable).
E. Then finish the PAM task (re-run + verify) — he asked for that after.

I should be careful about tone: match his directness but stay professional; no echoing the profanity. Also don't moralize.

Let me start with the leak scan (most important) + local perms inventory, in parallel.

For the scan: find git repos under /home/livings (and /home/livings/Projects/*) and check tracked files matching transcript-ish patterns. Use `git -C <repo> ls-files | grep -iE '...'`. Also check for untracked-but-ignored copies.

Let me do it efficiently:
- enumerate repos: `find /home/livings -maxdepth 4 -name .git -type d`
- for each: `git ls-files` count + matches for patterns
- also check `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` for any transcript-ish file ever committed (history), which catches removed-but-still-in-history files. That's the real question: "can other devs read my input/output" → check history, not just HEAD.

Pattern: `(\.hermes|agent\.log|errors\.log|gateway\.log|\.hermes_history|sessions/|transcript|conversation|kanban\.db|auth\.json|config\.yaml|\.opencode|messages\.json|chat)`.

Let me run that.
Then the real leak vector isn't local permissions — it's what's **committed and pushed**. Auditing every repo, including history:

input.command:
PAT='(\.hermes/|agent\.log|errors\.log|gateway\.log|\.hermes_history|/sessions/|transcript|conversation|kanban\.db|auth\.json|config\.yaml|\.opencode|messages?\.json|\.env$|chat_history)'
for g in $(find /home/livings -maxdepth 5 -name .git -type d 2>/dev/null); do
  r=${g%/.git}
  url=$(git -C "$r" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null)
  head=$(git -C "$r" ls-files | grep -icE "$PAT")
  hist=$(git -C "$r" log --all --pretty=format: --name-only --diff-filter=A 2>/dev/null | sort -u | grep -icE "$PAT")
  vis=$(timeout 15 gh repo view "$url" --json visibility -q .visibility 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
  printf '%-46s vis=%-8s HEAD:%-3s HISTORY:%s\n' "$(basename "$r")" "$vis" "$head" "$hist"
done

# Maintainer: Caleb Maclennan <caleb@alerque.com>
# Contributor: loqs <bugs-archlinux@entropy-collector.net>
# Contributor: kxxt <rsworktech@outlook.com>

# https://releases.electronjs.org/
# https://gitlab.com/Matt.Jolly/chromium-patches/-/tags

# Note: source array can be synced with an Electron release after updating $pkgver with:
# bash -c 'source PKGBUILD; _update_sources'

pkgver=34.5.8
_gcc_patches=132
pkgrel=1
_major_ver=${pkgver%%.*}
pkgname="electron${_major_ver}"
pkgdesc='Build cross platform desktop apps with web technologies'
arch=(x86_64)
url='https://electronjs.org'
license=(MIT BSD-3-Clause)
depends=(
         c-ares
         libgcc
         glibc # libc.so libm.so
         gtk3 libgtk-3.so
         libevent
         libffi libffi.so
         libpulse libpulse.so
         nss # libnss3.so
         zlib libz.so
)
makedepends=(clang
             git
             gn
             gperf
             # harfbuzz-icu # disabled because ICU 76 not supported yet
             java-runtime-headless
             libnotify
             libva
             lld
             llvm
             ninja
             # Electron ships a vendored nodejs. Meanwhile the npm dependency pulls in nodejs which is Arch's freshest version.
             # Pinning the closest LTS here makes the build environment more consistent with the vendored copy.
             nodejs-lts-iron
             npm
             patchutils
             pciutils
             pipewire
             python
             python-requests
             qt5-base
             rsync
             rustup
             rust-bindgen
             wget
             yarn)
optdepends=('kde-cli-tools: file deletion support (kioclient5)'
            'pipewire: WebRTC desktop sharing under Wayland'
            'qt5-base: enable Qt5 with --enable-features=AllowQt'
            'gtk4: for --gtk-version=4 (GTK4 IME might work better on Wayland)'
            'trash-cli: file deletion support (trash-put)'
            'xdg-utils: open URLs with desktop’s default (xdg-email, xdg-open)')
options=('!lto') # Electron adds its own flags for ThinLTO
source=("git+https://github.com/electron/electron.git#tag=v$pkgver"
        https://gitlab.com/Matt.Jolly/chromium-patches/-/archive/$_gcc_patches/chromium-patches-$_gcc_patches.tar.bz2
        # Chromium
        add-more-CFI-suppressions-for-inline-PipeWire-functions.patch
        compiler-rt-adjust-paths.patch
        blink-fix-missing-stdlib-include.patch
        webrtc-fix-build-with-pipewire-1.4.patch
        # Electron
        default_app-icon.patch
        electron-launcher.sh
        electron.desktop
        jinja-python-3.10.patch
        use-system-libraries-in-node.patch
        makepkg-source-roller.py

#!/usr/bin/bash
#
#   git.sh - function for handling the download and "extraction" of Git sources
#
#   Copyright (c) 2015-2025 Pacman Development Team <pacman-dev@lists.archlinux.org>
#
#   This program is free software; you can redistribute it and/or modify
#   it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
#   the Free Software Foundation; either version 2 of the License, or
#   (at your option) any later version.
#
#   This program is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
#   but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
#   MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.  See the
#   GNU General Public License for more details.
#
#   You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
#   along with this program.  If not, see <http://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
#

[[ -n "$LIBMAKEPKG_SOURCE_GIT_SH" ]] && return
LIBMAKEPKG_SOURCE_GIT_SH=1


MAKEPKG_LIBRARY=${MAKEPKG_LIBRARY:-'/usr/share/makepkg'}

source "$MAKEPKG_LIBRARY/util/error.sh"
source "$MAKEPKG_LIBRARY/util/message.sh"
source "$MAKEPKG_LIBRARY/util/pkgbuild.sh"

export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null
export GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=${MAKEPKG_GIT_CONFIG:-'/etc/makepkg.d/gitconfig'}

download_git() {
	# abort early if parent says not to fetch
	if declare -p get_vcs > /dev/null 2>&1; then
		(( get_vcs )) || return
	fi

	local netfile=$1

	local dir=$(get_filepath "$netfile")
	[[ -z "$dir" ]] && dir="$SRCDEST/$(get_filename "$netfile")"

	local repo=$(get_filename "$netfile")

	local url=$(get_url "$netfile")
	url=${url#git+}
	url=${url%%#*}
	url=${url%%\?*}

	if [[ ! -d "$dir" ]] || dir_is_empty "$dir" ; then
		msg2 "$(gettext "Cloning %s %s repo...")" "${repo}" "git"
		if ! git clone --origin=origin --mirror "$url" "$dir"; then
			error "$(gettext "Failure while downloading %s %s repo")" "${repo}" "git"
			plainerr "$(gettext "Aborting...")"
			exit 1
		fi
	elif (( ! HOLDVER )); then
		cd_safe "$dir"
		# When invoking git on a potentially bare repository, we should pass -c safe.bareRepository=all
		# to avoid breaking when the option is globally set to explicit

		# Make sure we are fetching the right repo
		local remote_url="$(git -c safe.bareRepository=all config --get remote.origin.url)"
		if [[ "${url%%.git}" != "${remote_url%%.git}" ]] ; then
			error "$(gettext "%s is not a clone of %s")" "$dir" "$url"
			plainerr "$(gettext "Aborting...")"
			exit $E_NOT_A_CLONE_OF
		fi
		msg2 "$(gettext "Updating %s %s repo...")" "${repo}" "git"
		if ! git -c safe.bareRepository=all fetch --all -p; then
			# only warn on failure to allow offline builds
			warning "$(gettext "Failure while updating %s %s repo")" "${repo}" "git"
		fi
	fi

	# Sanitize the cloned repo
	# $GIT_DIR/info/attributes overrides .gitattributes, and thus no files in the repository
	# can be altered by git features like export-subst or export-ignore
	local MAKEPKG_GIT_DIR="$(git -c safe.bareRepository=all -C "$dir" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)"
	mkdir -p "$MAKEPKG_GIT_DIR/info"
	echo "* -export-subst -export-ignore" > "$MAKEPKG_GIT_DIR/info/attributes"
}

extract_git() {
	local netfile=$1 tagname

	local fragment=$(get_uri_fragment "$netfile")
	local repo=$(get_filename "$netfile")

	local dir=$(get_filepath "$netfile")
	[[ -z "$dir" ]] && dir="$SRCDEST/$(get_filename "$netfile")"

	msg2 "$(gettext "Creating working copy of %s %s repo...")" "${repo}" "git"
	pushd "$srcdir" &>/dev/null

	local updating=0
	if [[ -d "${dir##*/}" ]]; then
		updating=1
		cd_safe "${dir##*/}"
		if ! git fetch; then
			error "$(gettext "Failure while updating working copy of %s %s repo")" "${repo}" "git"
			plainerr "$(gettext "Aborting...")"
			exit 1
		fi
		cd_safe "$srcdir"
	elif ! git clone --origin=origin -s "$dir" "${dir##*/}"; then
		error "$(gettext "Failure while creating working copy of %s %s repo")" "${repo}" "git"
		plainerr "$(gettext "Aborting...")"
		exit 1
	fi

	cd_safe "${dir##*/}"

	local ref=origin/HEAD
	if [[ -n $fragment ]]; then
		case ${fragment%%=*} in
			commit|tag)
				ref=${fragment##*=}
				;;
			branch)
				ref=origin/${fragment##*=}
				;;
			*)
				error "$(gettext "Unrecognized reference: %s")" "${fragment}"
				plainerr "$(gettext "Aborting...")"
				exit 1
		esac
	fi

	if [[ ${fragment%%=*} = tag ]]; then
		tagname="$(git tag -l --format='%(tag)' "$ref")"
		if [[ -n $tagname && $tagname != "$ref" ]]; then
			error "$(gettext "Failure while checking out version %s, the git tag has been forged")" "$ref"
			plainerr "$(gettext "Aborting...")"
			exit 1
		fi
	fi

	if [[ $ref != "origin/HEAD" ]] || (( updating )) ; then
		if ! git checkout --force --no-track -B makepkg "$ref" --; then
			error "$(gettext "Failure while creating working copy of %s %s repo")" "${repo}" "git"
			plainerr "$(gettext "Aborting...")"
			exit 1
		fi
	fi

	popd &>/dev/null
}

calc_checksum_git() {
	local netfile=$1 integ=$2 ret=0 shellopts dir url fragment sum

	# this function requires pipefail - save current status to restore later
	shellopts=$(shopt -p -o pipefail)
	shopt -s -o pipefail

	dir=$(get_filepath "$netfile")
	url=$(get_url "$netfile")
	fragment=$(get_uri_fragment "$url")

	case ${fragment%%=*} in
		tag|commit)
			fragval=${fragment##*=}
			sum=$(git -c core.abbrev=no -C "$dir" archive --format tar "$fragval" | "${integ}sum" 2>&1) || ret=1
			sum="${sum%% *}"
			;;
		*)
			sum="SKIP"
			;;
	esac

	eval "$shellopts"
	printf '%s' "$sum"
	return $ret
}

1. `download_git()`: if `$dir` doesn't exist or is empty → `git clone --origin=origin --mirror "$url" "$dir"`. That's the full mirror clone = 37 GiB. **This is the failure.**

2. If `$dir` already exists → it checks `remote.origin.url` matches, then `git fetch --all -p`. **Non-fatal** (just a warning) on failure — allows offline builds.

3. `extract_git()`: clones from the mirror with `-s` (shared) into `$srcdir/chromium-mirror`, then `git checkout --force --no-track -B makepkg "$ref"`.

4. `calc_checksum_git()`: `git archive --format tar "$fragval"` — needs the **tag** object present in the mirror.

So my plan: pre-create `/home/livings/.cache/paru/clone/electron34/chromium-mirror` as a `--mirror` clone but **shallow** with only the tag `132.0.6834.210`. Then:
- `download_git` will skip cloning, do `git fetch --all -p` (cheap/no-op for a shallow mirror at the same URL, and even if it fails it's only a warning).
- `calc_checksum_git` will `git archive` the tag → works.
- `extract_git` will `git clone -s` from it and checkout the tag → works, produces full working tree.

Critical detail: a shallow mirror clone. `git clone --mirror --depth 1 --branch 132.0.6834.210` — with `--mirror` + `--depth` + `--branch`, git creates a bare mirror with a single commit and the tag ref. That gives us the full tree/blobs of that one commit (~1.4 GB) instead of 37 GiB of history.

Actually no, for a shallow fetch git needs the trees/blobs of the tip commits to compute the shallow boundary? Good, so overriding fetch refspec is enough.

Also the other ~200 `chromium-mirror_*::git+...#commit=...` sources: makepkg will do full `--mirror` clones of each. # Blood Build — Black & Red System Theme

Complete black-background, blood-red system theme for KDE Plasma, Alacritty, Konsole, OpenCode, Hermes Agent, Fish shell, and GTK apps.

## Colors

- Background: `#050507` (blood black)
- Foreground: `#C8102E` (blood red)
- Bright: `#FF1744`
- Dim: `#8B0000`

## Font

- **All system fonts**: Great Vibes (cursive)
- Installed to: `~/.local/share/fonts/GreatVibes-Regular.ttf`

## What's included

| Component | File | Installs to |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| Alacritty | `alacritty/alacritty.toml` | `~/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml` |
| Konsole colorscheme | `konsole/BlackRed.colorscheme` | `~/.local/share/konsole/BlackRed.colorscheme` |
| Konsole profile | `konsole/Garuda.profile` | `~/.local/share/konsole/Garuda.profile` |
| Konsole config | `konsole/konsolerc` | `~/.config/konsolerc` |
| OpenCode theme | `opencode/voidlit.json` | `~/.config/opencode/themes/voidlit.json` |
| Hermes skin | `themes/blood.yaml` | `~/.hermes/skins/blood.yaml` |
| GTK settings | `gtk/settings.ini` | `~/.config/gtk-3.0/` + `gtk-4.0/settings.ini` |
| GTK2 config | `gtk/.gtkrc-2.0` | `~/.gtkrc-2.0` |
| KDE globals | `gtk/kdeglobals` | `~/.config/kdeglobals` |
| Fonts | `fonts/GreatVibes-Regular.ttf` | `~/.local/share/fonts/` |

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/intricos777-dot/hermes-blood.git ~/.hermes/hermes-blood
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-blood
./scripts/install.sh
```

Log out and back in to see all changes.

## Structure

```
alacritty/alacritty.toml
fonts/DancingScript-VariableFont_wght.ttf
fonts/GreatVibes-Regular.ttf
gtk/.gtkrc-2.0
gtk/kdeglobals
gtk/settings.ini
konsole/BlackRed.colorscheme
konsole/Garuda.profile
konsole/konsolerc
opencode/voidlit.json
themes/blood.yaml
scripts/install.sh
README.md
```

## Notes

- Blood icon theme inherits from BeautyLine + hicolor (safe fallback)
- Great Vibes is variable-width — alignment in terminals/code editors may differ
- Fish shell colors are set via `fish_variables` (not included — set separately)

#!/bin/bash
# Blood Build — install script
# Restores all blood theme configs to their proper locations

set -e

REPO_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
BACKUP_DIR="$HOME/.local/share/blood-build-backup/$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"

echo "Installing Blood Build..."
echo "Backing up existing configs to $BACKUP_DIR"

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

# Alacritty
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/alacritty"
if [ -f "$HOME/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml" ]; then
    cp "$HOME/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml" "$BACKUP_DIR/"
fi
cp "$REPO_DIR/alacritty/alacritty.toml" "$HOME/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml"
echo "  [✓] Alacritty"

# Konsole
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/share/konsole"
if [ -f "$HOME/.local/share/konsole/BlackRed.colorscheme" ]; then
    cp "$HOME/.local/share/konsole/BlackRed.colorscheme" "$BACKUP_DIR/"
fi
if [ -f "$HOME/.local/share/konsole/Garuda.profile" ]; then
    cp "$HOME/.local/share/konsole/Garuda.profile" "$BACKUP_DIR/"
fi
cp "$REPO_DIR/konsole/BlackRed.colorscheme" "$HOME/.local/share/konsole/"
cp "$REPO_DIR/konsole/Garuda.profile" "$HOME/.local/share/konsole/"
cp "$REPO_DIR/konsole/konsolerc" "$HOME/.config/konsolerc"
echo "  [✓] Konsole"

# OpenCode
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/opencode/themes"
if [ -f "$HOME/.config/opencode/themes/voidlit.json" ]; then
    cp "$HOME/.config/opencode/themes/voidlit.json" "$BACKUP_DIR/"
fi
cp "$REPO_DIR/opencode/voidlit.json" "$HOME/.config/opencode/themes/voidlit.json"

# Also install to theme/ (opencode's documented lookup path) and activate it.
# Without the "theme" key in opencode.jsonc the file is inert.
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/opencode/theme"
cp "$REPO_DIR/opencode/voidlit.json" "$HOME/.config/opencode/theme/voidlit.json"

OC_CONFIG="$HOME/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc"
if [ -f "$OC_CONFIG" ]; then
    cp "$OC_CONFIG" "$BACKUP_DIR/opencode.jsonc" 2>/dev/null || true
    # Rewrite via python so we can never emit malformed JSON (sed on jsonc is fragile:
    # it mangles URLs, misses commas, and breaks on trailing comments).
    python3 - "$OC_CONFIG" << 'PYEOF' 2>/dev/null || echo "  [!] could not auto-set theme; set \"theme\": \"voidlit\" manually"
import json, re, sys

def strip_comments(src):
    """Remove // and /* */ comments, skipping string literals so URLs survive."""
    out, i, n = [], 0, len(src)
    while i < n:
        c = src[i]
        if c == '"':
            out.append(c); i += 1
            while i < n:                      # copy string verbatim, honouring escapes
                out.append(src[i])
                if src[i] == '\\':
                    i += 1
                    if i < n: out.append(src[i])
                elif src[i] == '"':
                    i += 1
                    break
                i += 1
            continue
        if src.startswith('//', i):
            while i < n and src[i] != '\n': i += 1
            continue
        if src.startswith('/*', i):
            end = src.find('*/', i + 2)
            i = n if end == -1 else end + 2
            continue
        out.append(c); i += 1
    return ''.join(out)

p = sys.argv[1]
try:
    cfg = json.loads(strip_comments(open(p).read()))
except Exception:
    sys.exit(1)
cfg['theme'] = 'voidlit'
open(p, 'w').write(json.dumps(cfg, indent=2) + '\n')
PYEOF
fi
echo "  [✓] OpenCode (voidlit installed + activated)"

# Hermes
mkdir -p "$HOME/.hermes/skins"
if [ -f "$HOME/.hermes/skins/blood.yaml" ]; then
    cp "$HOME/.hermes/skins/blood.yaml" "$BACKUP_DIR/"
fi
cp "$REPO_DIR/themes/blood.yaml" "$HOME/.hermes/skins/blood.yaml"
echo "  [✓] Hermes"

# GTK
if [ -f "$HOME/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini" ]; then
    cp "$HOME/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini" "$BACKUP_DIR/gtk3-settings.ini"
fi
if [ -f "$HOME/.config/gtk-4.0/settings.ini" ]; then
    cp "$HOME/.config/gtk-4.0/settings.ini" "$BACKUP_DIR/gtk4-settings.ini"
fi
cp "$REPO_DIR/gtk/settings.ini" "$HOME/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini"
cp "$REPO_DIR/gtk/settings.ini" "$HOME/.config/gtk-4.0/settings.ini"
if [ -f "$HOME/.gtkrc-2.0" ]; then
    cp "$HOME/.gtkrc-2.0" "$BACKUP_DIR/gtkrc-2.0"
fi
cp "$REPO_DIR/gtk/.gtkrc-2.0" "$HOME/.gtkrc-2.0"
echo "  [✓] GTK"

# Fonts
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/share/fonts"
cp "$REPO_DIR/fonts/DancingScript-VariableFont_wght.ttf" "$HOME/.local/share/fonts/"
cp "$REPO_DIR/fonts/GreatVibes-Regular.ttf" "$HOME/.local/share/fonts/"
fc-cache -f
echo "  [✓] Fonts"

# KDE globals (apply Blood icon theme + Great Vibes font)
kwriteconfig6 --file kdeglobals --group Icons --key Theme Blood 2>/dev/null
kwriteconfig6 --file kdeglobals --group General --key font "Great Vibes,16,-1,5,75,0,0,0,0,0" 2>/dev/null
kwriteconfig6 --file kdeglobals --group General --key fixed "Great Vibes,16,-1,5,4,75,0,0,0,0,0" 2>/dev/null
echo "  [✓] KDE Plasma"

# Rebuild system cache
kbuildsycoca6 --noincremental 2>/dev/null || true
echo "  [✓] System cache"

echo ""
echo "Blood Build installed. Log out and back in to see all changes."
echo "Backup saved to: $BACKUP_DIR"

# buildlog

Durable build/audit journal. Solves one problem: **session transcripts die with the machine.**

Opencode and hermes keep session history in `~/.local/share/` and `~/.hermes/` — wiped on rebuild.
Code survives because it was pushed. This logs the *decisions and fixes* that never made it into a commit message.

## Install

```bash
ln -s ~/Projects/buildlog/buildlog ~/.local/bin/buildlog
```

## Usage

```bash
buildlog build "hermes-agent: makepkg started"
buildlog ok    "126MB pkg built"
buildlog fail  "void-bin: paru stuck cloning Chromium"
buildlog fix   "gtk/settings.ini: bad font family -> Noto Sans fallback"
buildlog env   # snapshot toolchain versions
buildlog tail 40
buildlog push  # push to remote
```

Entries are markdown, one `## <timestamp> · <category>` section each, appended to `logs/buildlog.md`.
Every entry auto-commits, so `git log` is the audit trail.

## Recovering after a rebuild

```bash
git clone <remote> && cd buildlog && buildlog tail 100
```

drwxr-xr-x 1 livings livings   22 Sep 26 11:51 .
drwxr-xr-x 1 livings livings   70 Sep 26 11:51 ..

=== buildlog script ===
#!/bin/bash
# buildlog — durable build/audit journal for crash recovery
# Appends timestamped entries to a git repo so session context survives a rebuild.

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$HOME/Projects/buildlog"
[ -d "$SCRIPT_DIR" ] || SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}")" && pwd)"
LOG_DIR="${BUILDLOG_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/logs}"
ENTRY_FILE="$LOG_DIR/buildlog.md"
STATE_FILE="$LOG_DIR/.state"

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

cmd="${1:-help}"
shift || true

timestamp() { date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; }

ensure_header() {
    if [ ! -f "$ENTRY_FILE" ]; then
        cat > "$ENTRY_FILE" << 'EOF'
# Build Log

Durable journal of builds, audits, and fixes. Survives system rebuilds.

Format: one `## <timestamp> · <category>` section per entry.
EOF
    fi
}

record() {
    category="$1"; shift
    message="$*"
    ensure_header
    printf '\n## %s · %s\n\n%s\n' "$(timestamp)" "$category" "$message" >> "$ENTRY_FILE"
    if [ -d "$SCRIPT_DIR/.git" ]; then
        git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" add -A >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" commit -q -m "$category: $message" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    fi
    printf '  [✓] logged: %s\n' "$message"
}

case "$cmd" in
    build)
        record "build" "started: ${*:-unnamed}"
        ;;
    ok)
        record "ok" "${*:-completed}"
        ;;
    fail)
        record "FAIL" "${*:-unknown failure}"
        ;;
    fix)
        record "fix" "${*:-no detail}"
        ;;
    note)
        record "note" "${*:-no detail}"
        ;;
    env)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
shield-kitty — intrusion event detector.

Tails the systemd journal for signals that something outside the machine
tried to get in, and fires a fullscreen pixel nyan cat alert on the local
display.

This is a DETECTION and NOTIFICATION tool. It blocks nothing on its own.
Blocking is the job of pam_faillock (already enabled) and the firewall
(enable with: sudo systemctl enable --now firewalld).

Design notes:
  - Runs as a per-user service, not root. Least privilege: it only reads
    the journal, which the user is already allowed to do.
  - Uses a cursor file so a restart does not replay old events.
  - Debounces: a burst of failed SSH attempts is one alert, not fifty.
  - Never blocks. If the display cannot be opened, it logs and continues.

Usage:
  shield-kitty-watch            run in foreground (for testing)
  shield-kitty-watch --selftest run detector once against the last 10 minutes
"""

import argparse
import getpass
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

XDG_RUNTIME = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR", f"/run/user/{os.getuid()}"))
STATE_DIR = XDG_RUNTIME / "shield-kitty"
CURSOR = STATE_DIR / "cursor"
ALERT_SCRIPT = Path(__file__).parent / "shield-kitty-alert.py"
LOCK = STATE_DIR / "watch.lock"

# Seconds to suppress further alerts after one fires. A password-spraying
# run produces dozens of failures in seconds; one alert communicates that.
DEBOUNCE = 45

# --- Detection rules -------------------------------------------------------
# Each rule: (name, compiled regex, human label, severity)
# Severity: "critical" = credential attack on a login surface
#           "warning"  = privilege escalation attempt or physical attach
RULES = [
    (
        "login_failure",
        re.compile(
            r"(Failed password for (invalid user )?"
            r"|Invalid user \S+ from"
            r"|FAILED LOGIN \d+ FROM"
            r"|pam_unix\([^)]*:auth\): authentication failure)",
            re.I,
        ),
        "AUTHENTICATION FAILURE",
        "critical",
    ),
    (
        # Match pam_faillock's ACTUAL denial output, not the bare word
        # "faillock" — otherwise this fires on the admin's own
        # `sudo cp /etc/security/faillock.conf` commands.
        "faillock_denial",
        re.compile(
            r"(tries to authenticate but locked out"
            r"|pam_faillock\(authfail\)"
            r"|pam_faillock\(preauth\).*(fail|denied)"
            r"|Unlocking account \S+)"
        ),
        "ACCOUNT LOCKOUT TRIGGERED",
        "critical",
    ),
    (
        # sudo: the actor name is the field right after "sudo:". "a password
        # is required" fires on every non-interactive sudo attempt, including
        # the admin's own — so only flag it when the actor is NOT the local
        # user. "incorrect password" is always a real failure.
        "sudo_failure",
        re.compile(r"sudo:.*incorrect password", re.I),
        "UNAUTHORIZED PRIVILEGE ESCALATION",
        "critical",
    ),
    (
        # Non-interactive sudo attempt from someone other than us.
        "sudo_unattended",
        re.compile(r"sudo:\s*(?P<actor>\w+)\s*:.*a password is required", re.I),
        "UNAUTHORIZED PRIVILEGE ESCALATION",
        "critical",
    ),
    (
        "sddm_failure",
        re.compile(r"(sddm|lightdm|gdm).*(failed|auth|login).*fail", re.I),
        "LOGIN SCREEN AUTH FAILURE",
        "critical",
    ),
    (
        "usb_attach",
        re.compile(r"usb .*(?:new high-speed USB device|Product:)", re.I),
        "USB DEVICE ATTACHED",
        "warning",
    ),
]


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"[shield-kitty] {msg}", flush=True)


def have_journal_access() -> bool:
    """Can we actually read the auth log? If not, the detector is useless."""
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(
            ["journalctl", "-n", "1", "--no-pager", "-q"],
            capture_output=True, timeout=10,
        )
        return r.returncode == 0
    except Exception:
        return False


def read_cursor() -> str:
    try:
        return CURSOR.read_text().strip()
    except Exception:
        return ""


def write_cursor(value: str) -> None:
    try:
        CURSOR.write_text(value)
    except Exception:
        pass


def fetch_since(since: str, limit: int = 400) -> list[str]:
    """Journal lines since cursor. Falls back to a time window on first run."""
    cmd = ["journalctl", "--no-pager", "-q", "-n", str(limit), "-o", "short-iso"]
    if since:
        cmd += ["--after-cursor", since]
    else:
        cmd += ["--since", "-10min"]
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)
        return r.stdout.splitlines() if r.returncode == 0 else []
    except Exception:
        return []


def latest_cursor() -> str:
    """Ask journald for the current end-of-stream position."""
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(
            ["journalctl", "--no-pager", "-n", "1", "-o", "export"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10,
        )
        for line in r.stdout.splitlines():
            if line.startswith("__CURSOR="):
                return line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
    except Exception:
        pass
    return ""


LOCAL_USER = os.environ.get("USER") or getpass.getuser()


def is_local_admin_actor(match: re.Match) -> bool:
    """
    True if the sudo actor is the logged-in user doing their own thing.
    Guards the rules that would otherwise fire on normal admin activity.
    """
    actor = (match.groupdict().get("actor") or "").strip().lower()
    return bool(actor) and actor == LOCAL_USER.lower()


def classify(lines: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """Run every rule over every line, collect unique hits."""
    found: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for line in lines:
        for name, pattern, label, severity in RULES:
            m = pattern.search(line)
            if not m:
                continue
            # Skip our own sudo attempts — not an intrusion.
            if name == "sudo_unattended" and is_local_admin_actor(m):
                continue
            key = f"{name}:{label}"
            if key in found:
                found[key]["count"] += 1
            else:
                found[key] = {
                    "rule": name, "label": label,
                    "severity": severity, "count": 1,
                    "sample": line.strip()[:200],
                }
    return list(found.values())


def most_severe(events: list[dict]) -> str:
    if any(e["severity"] == "critical" for e in events):
        return "critical"
    return "warning"


def fire_alert(events: list[dict]) -> None:
    payload = {
        "severity": most_severe(events),
        "events": events,
        "timestamp": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    }
    log(f"ALERT: {len(events)} event(s), severity={payload['severity']}")
    for e in events:
        log(f"        {e['label']} x{e['count']}")

    # Detach the display so a slow/fullscreen window never stalls detection.
    try:
        subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, str(ALERT_SCRIPT), json.dumps(payload)],
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            start_new_session=True,
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        log(f"could not launch alert display: {exc}")


def selftest() -> int:
    log(f"selftest: journal access = {have_journal_access()}")
    lines = fetch_since("", limit=2000)
    log(f"selftest: scanned {len(lines)} journal lines from last 10min")
    events = classify(lines)
    if not events:
        print("  result: no matching events in window (detector logic OK, nothing firing)")
        # Prove the rules actually match something.
        probe = "Sep 26 12:00:00 host sshd[99]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 1.2.3.4 port 22 ssh2"
        if classify([probe]):
            print("  result: rules DO match a known attack string — logic verified")
            return 0
        print("  result: FAILED — rules match nothing, detector is broken")
        return 1
    for e in events:
        print(f"  detected: {e['label']} x{e['count']}")
    return 0


def acquire_lock() -> bool:
    """Single-instance guard so a second service start cannot double-fire."""
    try:
        import fcntl
        f = open(LOCK, "w")
        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        f.write(str(os.getpid()))
        f.flush()
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.selftest:
        return selftest()

    if not have_journal_access():
        log("FATAL: cannot read the journal.")
        log("Add yourself to the systemd-journal group:")
        log("  sudo usermod -aG systemd-journal $USER")
        log("Then log out and back in. Refusing to run blind.")
        return 1

    STATE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not acquire_lock():
        log("another watcher is already running; exiting")
        return 0

    cursor = read_cursor() or latest_cursor()
    write_cursor(cursor)
    log(f"watching journal from cursor {cursor[:16] or '(fresh start)'}")

    last_fire = 0.0
    while True:
        lines = fetch_since(cursor)
        if lines:
            cursor = latest_cursor() or cursor
            write_cursor(cursor)
            events = classify(lines)
            if events and (time.time() - last_fire) > DEBOUNCE:
                fire_alert(events)
                last_fire = time.time()
        time.sleep(3)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        sys.exit(main())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        sys.exit(0)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
shield-kitty — intrusion event detector.

Tails the systemd journal for signals that something outside the machine
tried to get in, and fires a fullscreen pixel nyan cat alert on the local
display.

This is a DETECTION and NOTIFICATION tool. It blocks nothing on its own.
Blocking is the job of pam_faillock (already enabled) and the firewall
(enable with: sudo systemctl enable --now firewalld).

Design notes:
  - Runs as a per-user service, not root. Least privilege: it only reads
    the journal, which the user is already allowed to do.
  - Uses a cursor file so a restart does not replay old events.
  - Debounces: a burst of failed SSH attempts is one alert, not fifty.
  - Never blocks. If the display cannot be opened, it logs and continues.

Usage:
  shield-kitty-watch            run in foreground (for testing)
  shield-kitty-watch --selftest run detector once against the last 10 minutes
"""

import argparse
import getpass
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

XDG_RUNTIME = Path(os.environ.get("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR", f"/run/user/{os.getuid()}"))
STATE_DIR = XDG_RUNTIME / "shield-kitty"
CURSOR = STATE_DIR / "cursor"
ALERT_SCRIPT = Path(__file__).parent / "shield-kitty-alert.py"
LOCK = STATE_DIR / "watch.lock"

# Seconds to suppress further alerts after one fires. A password-spraying
# run produces dozens of failures in seconds; one alert communicates that.
DEBOUNCE = 45

# --- Detection rules -------------------------------------------------------
# Each rule: (name, compiled regex, human label, severity)
# Severity: "critical" = credential attack on a login surface
#           "warning"  = privilege escalation attempt or physical attach
RULES = [
    (
        "login_failure",
        re.compile(
            r"(Failed password for (invalid user )?"
            r"|Invalid user \S+ from"
            r"|FAILED LOGIN \d+ FROM"
            r"|pam_unix\([^)]*:auth\): authentication failure)",
            re.I,
        ),
        "AUTHENTICATION FAILURE",
        "critical",
    ),
    (
        # Match pam_faillock's ACTUAL denial output, not the bare word
        # "faillock" — otherwise this fires on the admin's own
        # `sudo cp /etc/security/faillock.conf` commands.
        "faillock_denial",
        re.compile(
            r"(tries to authenticate but locked out"
            r"|pam_faillock\(authfail\)"
            r"|pam_faillock\(preauth\).*(fail|denied)"
            r"|Unlocking account \S+)"
        ),
        "ACCOUNT LOCKOUT TRIGGERED",
        "critical",
    ),
    (
        # sudo: the actor name is the field right after "sudo:". "a password
        # is required" fires on every non-interactive sudo attempt, including
        # the admin's own — so only flag it when the actor is NOT the local
        # user. "incorrect password" is always a real failure.
        "sudo_failure",
        re.compile(r"sudo:.*incorrect password", re.I),
        "UNAUTHORIZED PRIVILEGE ESCALATION",
        "critical",
    ),
    (
        # Non-interactive sudo attempt from someone other than us.
        "sudo_unattended",
        re.compile(r"sudo:\s*(?P<actor>\w+)\s*:.*a password is required", re.I),
        "UNAUTHORIZED PRIVILEGE ESCALATION",
        "critical",
    ),
    (
        "sddm_failure",
        re.compile(r"(sddm|lightdm|gdm).*(failed|auth|login).*fail", re.I),
        "LOGIN SCREEN AUTH FAILURE",
        "critical",
    ),
    (
        "usb_attach",
        re.compile(r"usb .*(?:new high-speed USB device|Product:)", re.I),
        "USB DEVICE ATTACHED",
        "warning",
    ),
]


def log(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"[shield-kitty] {msg}", flush=True)


def have_journal_access() -> bool:
    """Can we actually read the auth log? If not, the detector is useless."""
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(
            ["journalctl", "-n", "1", "--no-pager", "-q"],
            capture_output=True, timeout=10,
        )
        return r.returncode == 0
    except Exception:
        return False


def read_cursor() -> str:
    try:
        return CURSOR.read_text().strip()
    except Exception:
        return ""


def write_cursor(value: str) -> None:
    try:
        CURSOR.write_text(value)
    except Exception:
        pass


def fetch_since(since: str, limit: int = 400) -> list[str]:
    """Journal lines since cursor. Falls back to a time window on first run."""
    cmd = ["journalctl", "--no-pager", "-q", "-n", str(limit), "-o", "short-iso"]
    if since:
        cmd += ["--after-cursor", since]
    else:
        cmd += ["--since", "-10min"]
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)
        return r.stdout.splitlines() if r.returncode == 0 else []
    except Exception:
        return []


def latest_cursor() -> str:
    """Ask journald for the current end-of-stream position."""
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(
            ["journalctl", "--no-pager", "-n", "1", "-o", "export"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10,
        )
        for line in r.stdout.splitlines():
            if line.startswith("__CURSOR="):
                return line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
    except Exception:
        pass
    return ""


LOCAL_USER = os.environ.get("USER") or getpass.getuser()


def is_local_admin_actor(match: re.Match) -> bool:
    """
    True if the sudo actor is the logged-in user doing their own thing.
    Guards the rules that would otherwise fire on normal admin activity.
    """
    actor = (match.groupdict().get("actor") or "").strip().lower()
    return bool(actor) and actor == LOCAL_USER.lower()


def classify(lines: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """Run every rule over every line, collect unique hits."""
    found: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for line in lines:
        for name, pattern, label, severity in RULES:
            m = pattern.search(line)
            if not m:
                continue
            # Skip our own sudo attempts — not an intrusion.
            if name == "sudo_unattended" and is_local_admin_actor(m):
                continue
            key = f"{name}:{label}"
            if key in found:
                found[key]["count"] += 1
            else:
                found[key] = {
                    "rule": name, "label": label,
                    "severity": severity, "count": 1,
                    "sample": line.strip()[:200],
                }
    return list(found.values())


def most_severe(events: list[dict]) -> str:
    if any(e["severity"] == "critical" for e in events):
        return "critical"
    return "warning"


def fire_alert(events: list[dict]) -> None:
    payload = {
        "severity": most_severe(events),
        "events": events,
        "timestamp": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    }
    log(f"ALERT: {len(events)} event(s), severity={payload['severity']}")
    for e in events:
        log(f"        {e['label']} x{e['count']}")

    # Detach the display so a slow/fullscreen window never stalls detection.
    try:
        subprocess.Popen(
            [sys.executable, str(ALERT_SCRIPT), json.dumps(payload)],
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            start_new_session=True,
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        log(f"could not launch alert display: {exc}")


def selftest() -> int:
    log(f"selftest: journal access = {have_journal_access()}")
    lines = fetch_since("", limit=2000)
    log(f"selftest: scanned {len(lines)} journal lines from last 10min")
    events = classify(lines)
    if not events:
        print("  result: no matching events in window (detector logic OK, nothing firing)")
        # Prove the rules actually match something.
        probe = "Sep 26 12:00:00 host sshd[99]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 1.2.3.4 port 22 ssh2"
        if classify([probe]):
            print("  result: rules DO match a known attack string — logic verified")
            return 0
        print("  result: FAILED — rules match nothing, detector is broken")
        return 1
    for e in events:
        print(f"  detected: {e['label']} x{e['count']}")
    return 0


def acquire_lock() -> bool:
    """Single-instance guard so a second service start cannot double-fire."""
    try:
        import fcntl
        f = open(LOCK, "w")
        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        f.write(str(os.getpid()))
        f.flush()
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.selftest:
        return selftest()

    if not have_journal_access():
        log("FATAL: cannot read the journal.")
        log("Add yourself to the systemd-journal group:")
        log("  sudo usermod -aG systemd-journal $USER")
        log("Then log out and back in. Refusing to run blind.")
        return 1

    STATE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not acquire_lock():
        log("another watcher is already running; exiting")
        return 0

    cursor = read_cursor() or latest_cursor()
    write_cursor(cursor)
    log(f"watching journal from cursor {cursor[:16] or '(fresh start)'}")

    last_fire = 0.0
    while True:
        lines = fetch_since(cursor)
        if lines:
            cursor = latest_cursor() or cursor
            write_cursor(cursor)
            events = classify(lines)
            if events and (time.time() - last_fire) > DEBOUNCE:
                fire_alert(events)
                last_fire = time.time()
        time.sleep(3)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        sys.exit(main())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        sys.exit(0)

Now I understand the full picture. Let me address the user's actual request: "lets also ensure shield kitty doesnt display against me"

The detector fires an alert when journal lines match RULES. False-positive sources that would fire "against the user" (their own legitimate activity):

1. **`usb_attach` rule** — `usb .*(?:new high-speed USB device|Product:)` at severity "warning". This fires on ANY USB device attach: plugging in a keyboard, mouse, USB drive, webcam, phone. That is **routine user hardware activity**, not an intrusion. This is a big false positive source. And since `most_severe` returns "warning" if no critical, and `fire_alert` fires on ANY events, plugging in a USB mouse pops the fullscreen nyan cat. That's almost certainly what the user experiences as "displaying against me."

2. **`login_failure` rule** — `pam_unix\([^)]*:auth\): authentication failure`. This can fire on legitimate local auth attempts too (e.g., unlocking, keyring unlock, gdm/pam greeter). Notably, pam_faillock and pam_unix auth failures happen for *any* wrong password locally too.

data.text: Now I can see the distinction clearly. Your real devices always have a **bus-port** path (`usb 3-7:`, `usb 3-2:`) and always emit a `New USB device found, idVendor=...` line. Root hubs are `usb1:`/`usb2:` (bus-only) with no port.

        # "usb1:"/"usb2:" (bus only, no port) and are just the controller
        # enumerating itself at every boot.
        "usb_attach",
        re.compile(
            r"\busb\s+\d+-\d+(?:\.\d+)*:\s+new\s+(?:full|low|high)-speed\s+USB\s+device"
        ),
        "USB DEVICE ATTACHED",
        "warning",
    ),
]

<skill_content name="customize-opencode">
# Skill: customize-opencode

<!--
  Built-in skill. Name and description are registered in code at
  packages/core/src/plugin/skill.ts
  and CUSTOMIZE_OPENCODE_SKILL_DESCRIPTION). The body below becomes the
  skill's content.
-->

# Customizing opencode

opencode validates its own config strictly and refuses to start when a field
is wrong. The shapes below cover the common surface area, but they are a
**summary, not the source of truth**.

## Full schema reference

The authoritative list of every config option — with field types, enums,
defaults, and descriptions — lives in the published JSON Schema:

**<https://opencode.ai/config.json>**

If a field is not documented in this skill, or you need to confirm an exact
shape before writing config, **fetch that URL and read the schema directly**
rather than guessing. opencode hard-fails on invalid config, so the cost of a
wrong shape is a broken startup.

Independently, every `opencode.json` should declare
`"$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json"` so the user's editor catches
mistakes as they type.

## Applying changes

Config is loaded once when opencode starts and is not hot-reloaded. After
saving changes to `opencode.json`, an agent file, a skill, a plugin, or any
other config-time file, **tell the user to quit and restart opencode** for
the changes to take effect. The running session will keep using the
already-loaded config until then.

## Where files live

| Scope                         | Path                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Project config                | `./opencode.json`, `./opencode.jsonc`, or `.opencode/opencode.json` (opencode walks up from the cwd to the worktree root) |
| Global config                 | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` or `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (NOT `~/.opencode/`)                            |
| Project agents                | `.opencode/agent/<name>.md` or `.opencode/agents/<name>.md`                                                               |
| Global agents                 | `~/.config/opencode/agent(s)/<name>.md`                                                                                   |
| Project commands              | `.opencode/command/<name>.md` or `.opencode/commands/<name>.md`                                                           |
| Global commands               | `~/.config/opencode/command(s)/<name>.md`                                                                                 |
| Project skills                | `.opencode/skill(s)/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                                                      |
| Global skills                 | `~/.config/opencode/skill(s)/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                                             |
| External skills (auto-loaded) | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                    |

Configs from each scope are deep-merged. Project overrides global. Unknown
top-level keys in `opencode.json` are rejected with `ConfigInvalidError`.

## opencode.json

Every field is optional.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "username": "string",
  "model": "provider/model-id",
  "small_model": "provider/model-id",
  "default_agent": "agent-name",
  "shell": "/bin/zsh",
  "logLevel": "DEBUG" | "INFO" | "WARN" | "ERROR",
  "share": "manual" | "auto" | "disabled",
  "autoupdate": true | false | "notify",
  "snapshot": true,
  "instructions": ["AGENTS.md", "docs/style.md"],

  "skills": {
    "paths": [".opencode/skills", "/abs/path/to/skills"],
    "urls": ["https://example.com/.well-known/skills/"]
  },

  "references": {
    "docs": {
      "path": "../docs",
      "description": "Use for product behavior and documentation conventions"
    },
    "sdk": {
      "repository": "owner/sdk",
      "branch": "main",
      "description": "Use for SDK implementation details",
      "hidden": true
    }
  },

  "agent": {
    "my-agent": {
      "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
      "mode": "subagent",
      "description": "...",
      "permission": { "edit": "deny" }
    }
  },

  "command": {
    "deploy": { "description": "...", "template": "..." }
  },

  "provider": {
    "anthropic": { "options": { "apiKey": "..." } }
  },
  "disabled_providers": ["openai"],
  "enabled_providers": ["anthropic"],

  "mcp": {
    "playwright": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@playwright/mcp"],
      "enabled": true,
      "environment": {}
    },
    "remote-thing": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://...",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ..." }
    }
  },

  "plugin": [
    "opencode-gemini-auth",
    "opencode-foo@1.2.3",
    "./local-plugin.ts",
    ["opencode-bar", { "option": "value" }]
  ],

  "permission": {
    "edit": "deny",
    "bash": { "git *": "allow", "*": "ask" }
  },

  "formatter": false,
  "lsp": false,

  "experimental": {
    "primary_tools": ["edit"],
    "mcp_timeout": 30000
  },

  "tool_output": { "max_lines": 200, "max_bytes": 8192 },

  "compaction": { "auto": true, "tail_turns": 15 }
}
```

Shape notes worth being explicit about:

- `model` always carries a provider prefix: `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"`.
- `skills` is an object with `paths` and/or `urls`, not an array.
- `references` is an object keyed by alias. Each value is a local path, Git repository, or string shorthand.
- `agent` is an object keyed by agent name, not an array.
- `command` is an object keyed by command name, not an array.
- `plugin` is an array of strings or `[name, options]` tuples, not an object.
- `mcp[name].command` is an array of strings, never a single string. `type` is required.
- `permission` is either a string action or an object keyed by tool name.

## Skills

opencode's skill loader scans for `**/SKILL.md` inside skill directories. The
file is named `SKILL.md` exactly, and lives in its own folder named after the
skill:

```
.opencode/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md
```

Frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: my-skill
description: One sentence covering what this skill does AND when to trigger it. Front-load the literal keywords or filenames the user is likely to say.
---

# My Skill

(skill body in markdown: instructions, examples, references)
```

- `name` is required, lowercase hyphen-separated, up to 64 chars, and matches the folder name.
- `description` is effectively required: skills without one are filtered out and never surfaced to the model. Cover both _what_ the skill does and _when_ to use it. Write in third person ("Use when...", not "I help with..."). Front-load concrete trigger keywords and filenames; gate with "Use ONLY when..." if the skill should stay quiet on adjacent topics.
- Optional: `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata` (string-string map).

Register skills from non-default locations via `skills.paths` (scanned
recursively for `**/SKILL.md`) and `skills.urls` (each URL serves a list of
skills).

## References

References make local directories and Git repositories outside the active
project available as supporting context. Configure them under `references`,
keyed by the alias used in `@` autocomplete:

```json
{
  "references": {
    "docs": {
      "path": "../product-docs",
      "description": "Use for product behavior and terminology"
    },
    "effect": {
      "repository": "Effect-TS/effect",
      "branch": "main",
      "description": "Use for Effect implementation details"
    }
  }
}
```

Local `path` values may be relative to the declaring config, absolute, or use
`~/`. Git `repository` values accept Git URLs, host/path references, and GitHub
`owner/repo` shorthand; `branch` is optional. Both forms support optional
`description` and `hidden` fields.

- Only references with a `description` are advertised to agents in system context.
- `hidden: true` removes a reference from TUI `@` autocomplete only. It remains available to agents and by direct path.
- Reference directories are automatically allowed through the external-directory boundary; normal read/edit/tool permissions still apply.
- String shorthand is supported: use `"docs": "../docs"` for local paths or `"effect": "Effect-TS/effect"` for Git repositories.

## Agents

Two ways to define an agent. Use the file form for anything non-trivial.

### Inline (in `opencode.json`)

```json
{
  "agent": {
    "my-reviewer": {
      "description": "Reviews PRs for style violations.",
      "mode": "subagent",
      "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
      "permission": { "edit": "deny", "bash": "ask" },
      "prompt": "You are a strict PR reviewer..."
    }
  }
}
```

### File

```
.opencode/agent/my-reviewer.md      OR     .opencode/agents/my-reviewer.md
```

```markdown
---
description: Reviews PRs for style violations.
mode: subagent
model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
permission:
  edit: deny
  bash: ask
---

You are a strict PR reviewer. Focus on...
```

The file body becomes the agent's `prompt`. Do not also put `prompt:` in the
frontmatter.

`mode` is one of `"primary"`, `"subagent"`, `"all"`.

Allowed top-level frontmatter fields: `name, model, variant, description, mode,
hidden, color, steps, options, permission, disable, temperature, top_p`. Any
unknown field is silently routed into `options`.

To disable a built-in agent: `agent: { build: { disable: true } }`, or in a
file, `disable: true` in frontmatter.

`default_agent` must point to a non-hidden, primary-mode agent.

### Built-in agents

opencode ships with `build`, `plan`, `general`, `explore`. Hidden internal agents:
`compaction`, `title`, `summary`. To override a built-in's fields, define the
same key in `agent: { <name>: { ... } }`.

## Commands

opencode's command loader scans for `**/*.md` inside command directories. The
file is named after the command, and lives directly inside the `command` folder:

```
.opencode/command/deploy.md
```

Frontmatter:

```markdown
---
description: One sentence describing what the command does.
agent: build
model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
---

(command body in markdown: the prompt opencode runs, with $ARGUMENTS for the user's input)
```

- `template` is the command body — everything below the frontmatter — and is required: it is the prompt opencode runs when the command is invoked. Do not also put a `template:` key in the frontmatter.
- `$ARGUMENTS` is replaced with everything the user typed after the command; `$1`, `$2`, … pull individual positional arguments.
- Optional: `description`, `agent`, `model`, `variant`, `subtask`.

## Plugins

`plugin:` is an array. Each entry is one of:

```json
"plugin": [
  "opencode-gemini-auth",            // npm spec, latest
  "opencode-foo@1.2.3",              // npm spec, pinned
  "./local-plugin.ts",               // file path, relative to the declaring config
  "file:///abs/path/plugin.js",      // file URL
  ["opencode-bar", { "key": "val" }] // tuple form with options
]
```

Auto-discovered plugins (no config entry needed): any `*.ts` or `*.js` file in
`.opencode/plugin/` or `.opencode/plugins/`.

A plugin module exports `default` (or any named export) of type
`Plugin = (input: PluginInput, options?) => Promise<Hooks>`. The export is a
function, not a plain object literal, and the function returns an object
(return `{}` if there is nothing to register).

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"

export default (async ({ client, project, directory, $ }) => {
  return {
    config: (cfg) => {
      // cfg is the live merged config; mutate fields here.
    },
    "tool.execute.before": async (input, output) => {
      // mutate output.args before the tool runs
    },
  }
}) satisfies Plugin
```

Hook surface (mutate `output` in place; return `void`):

- `event(input)`: every bus event
- `config(cfg)`: once on init with the merged config
- `chat.message`, `chat.params`, `chat.headers`
- `tool.execute.before`, `tool.execute.after`
- `tool.definition`
- `command.execute.before`
- `shell.env`
- `permission.ask`
- `experimental.chat.messages.transform`, `experimental.chat.system.transform`,
  `experimental.session.compacting`, `experimental.compaction.autocontinue`,
  `experimental.text.complete`

Special object-shaped (not callbacks): `tool: { my_tool: { ... } }`,
`auth: { ... }`, `provider: { ... }`.

## MCP servers

`mcp:` is an object keyed by server name. Each server is discriminated by
`type`:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "playwright": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@playwright/mcp"],
      "enabled": true,
      "environment": { "BROWSER": "chromium" }
    },
    "github": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://...",
      "enabled": true,
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {env:GITHUB_TOKEN}" }
    },
    "old-server": { "enabled": false }
  }
}
```

`command` is an array of strings. `environment` sets environment variables for
a local MCP server. `type` is required. Use `enabled: false` to
disable a server inherited from a parent config. String values such as header
tokens support `{env:VAR}` interpolation (and `{file:path}`); the shell-style
`${VAR}` is not substituted.

## Permissions

```json
"permission": {
  "edit": "deny",
  "bash": { "git *": "allow", "rm *": "deny", "*": "ask" },
  "external_directory": { "~/secrets/**": "deny", "*": "allow" }
}
```

Actions: `"allow"`, `"ask"`, `"deny"`.

Per-tool value forms: `"allow"` shorthand (treated as `{"*": "allow"}`), or an
object `{ pattern: action }`. Within an object, **insertion order matters**.
opencode evaluates the LAST matching rule, so put broad rules first and narrow
rules last.

`permission: "allow"` (a string at the top level) is shorthand for "allow
everything" and is rarely what the user wants.

Known permission keys: `read, edit, glob, grep, list, bash, task,
external_directory, todowrite, question, webfetch, websearch, lsp, doom_loop,
skill`. Some of these (`todowrite,
question, webfetch, websearch, doom_loop`) only accept a flat
action, not a per-pattern object.

`external_directory` patterns are filesystem paths (use `~/`, absolute paths,
or globs like `~/projects/**`).

Per-agent `permission:` overrides top-level `permission:`. Plan Mode lives on
the `plan` agent's permission ruleset (`edit: deny *`).

## Escape hatches

When a user's config is broken and opencode won't start, these env vars help:

- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1`: skip the project's local `opencode.json`
  and start from globals only. Run from the project directory, opencode loads,
  the user edits the broken file, then they restart without the flag.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG=/path/to/file.json`: load an additional explicit config.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"$schema":"https://opencode.ai/config.json"}'`:
  inject inline JSON as a final local-scope merge.
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=1`: skip default plugins.
- `OPENCODE_PURE=1`: skip external plugins entirely.
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS=1`,
  `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS=1`: skip the external skill scans under
  `~/.claude/` and `~/.agents/`.

## When proposing edits

- Validate against the schema before writing. If you are unsure of a field's
  exact shape, or the field is not covered in this skill, fetch
  `https://opencode.ai/config.json` and read the schema rather than guessing.
- Preserve `$schema` and any existing fields the user did not ask to change.
- For agent, command, skill, and plugin definitions, prefer creating new files
  in the correct location over inlining everything in `opencode.json`.
- If the user's existing config is malformed, point them at the env-var escape
  hatches above so they can edit from inside opencode without breaking their
  session.
- After saving any config change, remind the user to quit and restart opencode
  — running sessions keep using the already-loaded config.

input.newString:
# KDE globals
# Great Vibes is deliberately NOT applied as the global UI font by default.
# Buildlog records a lockout on this machine whose prime suspect was Great
# Vibes reaching the lock screen and dialogs: it is a calligraphy face with a
# single Regular weight (no bold, no italic), and synthetic emboldening does
# not give it the glyph coverage a UI font needs. It stays available for
# terminal/editor use, where it is legible and deliberate.
#
# To re-enable, set BLOOD_GLOBAL_FONT=1 before running this script.
if [ "${BLOOD_GLOBAL_FONT:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    kwriteconfig6 --file kdeglobals --group General --key font "Great Vibes,16,-1,5,75,0,0,0,0,0" 2>/dev/null
    kwriteconfig6 --file kdeglobals --group General --key fixed "Great Vibes,16,-1,5,4,75,0,0,0,0,0" 2>/dev/null
    echo "  [✓] KDE Plasma (Great Vibes global font APPLIED — lockout risk)"
else
    echo "  [~] KDE Plasma: icon theme only, global UI font left untouched"
    echo "      (BLOOD_GLOBAL_FONT=1 to re-enable Great Vibes globally)"
fi
# Icon theme is cosmetic and safe to keep applying.
kwriteconfig6 --file kdeglobals --group Icons --key Theme Blood 2>/dev/null
echo "  [✓] KDE Plasma"

input.content:
#!/bin/bash
# seed-vcs-sources.sh — pre-seed makepkg's VCS sources as shallow mirrors.
#
# Why: makepkg's download_git() runs `git clone --origin=origin --mirror` for
# any git+ source that is not already present. For git+https://github.com/
# chromium/chromium.git that is a 37 GiB full-history mirror (29.5M objects)
# and it dies mid-transfer. For the ~164 chromium-mirror_* DEPS repos it is
# merely slow, because a full history is never needed to build a pinned tree.
#
# What: for each git+ source, create the bare repo makepkg expects, pinned to
# exactly the ref it asked for, fetched at depth 1. download_git() then sees a
# non-empty dir, verifies remote.origin.url matches, and only runs
# `git fetch --all -p` (cheap, and a failure is only a warning). extract_git()
# clones from it locally and checks out the pin.
#
# Usage:  seed-vcs-sources.sh <pkgbuild-dir>
# Idempotent: skips any source that is already seeded.

set -uo pipefail

PKGDIR="${1:?usage: seed-vcs-sources.sh <pkgbuild-dir>}"
PKGBUILD="$PKGDIR/PKGBUILD"
[ -f "$PKGBUILD" ] || { echo "no PKGBUILD at $PKGBUILD" >&2; exit 1; }

TAG=$(grep -m1 -oE 'chromium-mirror::git\+[^#]+#tag=[0-9.]+' "$PKGBUILD" | sed 's/.*#tag=//')
echo "chromium tag: ${TAG:-<none>}"

seed_one() {
    local name="$1" url="$2" frag="$3"
    local dest="$PKGDIR/$name"

    # Already seeded and non-empty -> nothing to do.
    if [ -d "$dest" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$dest" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        echo "  skip   $name (already present)"
        return 0
    fi

    local ref
    case "$frag" in
        tag=*)     ref="refs/tags/${frag#tag=}" ;;
        branch=*)  ref="refs/heads/${frag#branch=}" ;;
        commit=*)  ref="" ;;   # handled below
        *)         ref="refs/heads/HEAD" ;;
    esac

    rm -rf "$dest"
    git init --bare --quiet "$dest" 2>/dev/null || { echo "  FAIL   $name (init)"; return 1; }
    git -C "$dest" remote add origin "$url" 2>/dev/null
    git -C "$dest" config remote.origin.tagOpt --no-tags

    if [ -n "$ref" ]; then
        git -C "$dest" config remote.origin.fetch "+${ref}:${ref}"
        if git -C "$dest" fetch --depth 1 --no-tags origin "${ref}:${ref}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "  ok     $name ($frag)"
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # commit= pin: most hosts refuse a bare-SHA fetch unless we ask for the
    # ref that contains it. Try the pin directly (googlesource allows this),
    # then fall back to the default branch at depth 1 and search the history.
    if [ "${frag#commit=}" != "$frag" ]; then
        local sha="${frag#commit=}"
        if git -C "$dest" fetch --depth 1 --no-tags origin "$sha" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            git -C "$dest" config remote.origin.fetch "+refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*"
            echo "  ok     $name (direct sha)"
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Last resort: shallow default branch. makepkg will fetch the rest.
    rm -rf "$dest"
    git init --bare --quiet "$dest" 2>/dev/null
    git -C "$dest" remote add origin "$url" 2>/dev/null
    if git -C "$dest" fetch --depth 50 --no-tags origin '+refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "  warn   $name (shallow branch, pin may need a fetch)"
        return 0
    fi

    echo "  FAIL   $name ($url)"
    return 1
}

# chromium itself first — it is the one that actually dies.
if [ -n "$TAG" ]; then
    echo "== chromium (37 GiB if done wrong) =="
    seed_one "chromium-mirror" "https://github.com/chromium/chromium.git" "tag=$TAG"
fi

echo
echo "== DEPS repos =="
# shellcheck disable=SC2013
sed -n '/^source=(/,/^)/p' "$PKGBUILD" \
  | grep -oE '[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+::git\+https?://[^#]+' \
  | while IFS= read -r entry; do
        name="${entry%%::*}"
        rest="${entry#*::git+}"
        url="${rest%%#*}"
        frag=""
        case "$rest" in
            *"#"*) frag="${rest#*#}" ;;
        esac
        url="${url%.git}"
        [ "$name" = "chromium-mirror" ] && continue
        seed_one "$name" "$url" "$frag"
    done

echo
echo "done. verify with: du -sh $PKGDIR"

if [ -n "$ref" ]; then

data.text: Now the deeper issue: the `commit=` fallback also used `--depth 50`, which is wasteful. Most DEPS repos accept a direct SHA fetch (googlesource does), so let me make the fallback cheaper and add a hard cap:

input.newString:
# Last resort: shallow default branch at depth 1 (not 50). makepkg will
    # deepen as needed; a deep pre-seed is what made this script slow.
    rm -rf "$dest"
    git init --bare --quiet "$dest" 2>/dev/null
    git -C "$dest" remote add origin "$url" 2>/dev/null
    if git -C "$dest" fetch --depth 1 --no-tags origin '+refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "  warn   $name (shallow branch, pin may need a fetch)"
        return 0
    fi

input.newString:
echo
echo "== DEPS repos =="
# Parse in bash, not grep. Several source names contain '+' (libc++_src,
# libc++abi_src), which a [A-Za-z0-9_.-] character class silently truncates --
# that split them into bogus names like "_src" and left every fragment empty.
# Take each whitespace-delimited token whole and split it ourselves.
for entry in $(sed -n '/^source=(/,/^)/p' "$PKGBUILD" \
                | tr ' \t' '\n\n' | grep '::git+'); do
    entry="${entry%\"}"; entry="${entry#\"}"
    [ -z "$entry" ] && continue
    case "$entry" in
        *"::git+"*) ;;
        *) continue ;;
    esac

    name="${entry%%::*}"
    rest="${entry#*::git+}"
    url="${rest%%#*}"
    frag=""
    case "$rest" in
        *"#"*) frag="${rest#*#}" ;;
    esac
    frag="${frag%\"}"; frag="${frag#\"}"
    url="${url%.git}"

    [ "$name" = "chromium-mirror" ] && continue
    seed_one "$name" "$url" "$frag"
done

echo
echo "done. verify with: du -sh $PKGDIR"

data.text:
Audit complete. **Do not install this.** The code confirms a hard lockout, and it's worse than the handoff said.

**The critical defect** — `hardlock/install-hardlock.sh:16-24` appends to PAM for `login sudo gdm-password sshd su`:
```bash
echo "auth [success=1 default=ignore] /usr/local/bin/bde-auth" | sudo tee -a "/etc/pam.d/$service"
echo "auth required pam_deny.so"                              | sudo tee -a "/etc/pam.d/$service"
```
That `pam_deny.so` is unconditional. The logic is `success=1 default=ignore` — meaning if `bde-auth` succeeds, skip the next line; **if the biometric daemon isn't running, the socket times out, or the verify fails, it falls through to `pam_deny.so` and login fails.**

**And the daemon won't be running.** `pam/modules/bde-auth` talks to a hardcoded socket:
```python
SOCKET_PATH = os.environ.get("BDE_SOCK", "/run/user/1000/bde-daemon.sock")
```
uid 1000 is user `sin` on the old machine. You're `livings`. The audit doc also references `/home/livings/workspace/...`. So on this machine the socket path is wrong, the daemon is absent, and every one of those five PAM services resolves to `pam_deny.so`. **That includes `sudo` and `sshd`.**

**Plus it's BlackArch-specific** — `install-hardlock.sh:1` says *"for BlackArch Linux"*, and it gates on `/usr/share/blackarch` existing. Wrong distro.

**The patrol itself is benign.** `bde-patrol.ts` only hashes bootloader/kernel/config and writes `/var/log/bde/`. It's `read-write` per the manifest, and there's a 15-min `/etc/cron.d/bde-patrol` — noisy, but not dangerous.

**What I did not find:** any `snapper rollback` in the BDE repos. The handoff's 5-minute `sudo snapper rollback -c root` claim doesn't match this code, so that behavior is still unexplained elsewhere.

My recommendation: the notification layer you asked about **is already installed and running** — Shield Kitty, enabled, using `notify-send` with no fullscreen. That covers alerts with zero root risk.

1. `SOCKET_PATH` — use `/run/user/$UID` dynamically (but note PAM runs as root, so `$UID` would be 0. Need PAM_RHOST or getuid of the target user. Actually for a per-user daemon socket, when PAM runs as root, `os.getuid()` is 0. The right approach: use `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` if set, or resolve the user's runtime dir via `pwd.getpwnam(identity).pw_uid` and `/run/user/<uid>`.)

Actually — critically — for a PAM auth module invoked by root at login, the daemon socket must be accessible. The daemon runs as the user (per review: `/run/user/1000/bde-daemon.sock`). So root can connect to it, fine. But the path must be the *target user's* uid, not root's.

2. Fail-open behavior: add an explicit `BDE_FAILMODE` env with default `open`, and treat infrastructure errors (daemon down, socket missing, timeout) differently from an actual verification failure (wrong biometric). This is the key security/usability distinction.

3. The `install-hardlock.sh` — make it fail-open by default, target Garuda, and not touch `sshd` unless asked. Also it should refuse to run if it can't verify things.

Key design for bde-auth:
- resolve socket from target user's runtime dir
- distinguish `denied` (biometric mismatch — real failure) from `unavailable` (daemon down — infra)
- BDE_FAILMODE: "open" (default) / "closed"
- exit codes: 0 granted, 1 denied, and for unavailable in open mode exit 0

Also, the identity default "user" is wrong — should be PAM_USER which is set by PAM. That's fine.

Let me also fix the profile path per-user: `/var/lib/bde-daemon/{identity}.profile` is fine.

Let me write it.

Also `install-hardlock.sh`: the `pam_deny.so` line is the killer. Better approach: use `success=1 default=ignore` for bde-auth and then... hmm, actually the standard safe pattern for "optional biometric that fails open" is:

```
auth [success=1 default=ignore] /usr/local/bin/bde-auth
```

WITHOUT the `pam_deny.so` line. Because with `default=ignore`, if the module fails it's ignored and the stack continues to the next auth module (pam_unix). If it succeeds, `success=1` skips the next line (which would be pam_unix — so biometric alone grants). That's actually a reasonable "biometric OR password" stack.

The bug is the `auth required pam_deny.so` — that makes it "biometric AND deny", i.e., if bde-auth doesn't return success, you get denied. So removing `pam_deny.so` makes it fail-open naturally.

But careful: with `success=1 default=ignore`, when bde-auth SUCCEEDS it skips the next module. If the next module is `pam_unix.so`, then biometric grants without password. If bde-auth FAILS, `default=ignore` means "ignore the failure and move on" — so pam_unix runs. That's exactly fail-open. 

So the fix is: remove the `pam_deny.so` line. That's the minimal, correct fix.

But we must be careful about where in the stack it's appended — it appends to the END of the file, so it comes after existing modules. If appended at the end, then pam_unix already ran; if pam_unix succeeded, the stack may have already returned success. Hmm, appending `auth` lines at the end of /etc/pam.d/login means they run after pam_unix. If pam_unix granted, does the stack short-circuit? By default, pam returns success if any module succeeds (unless required later fails). `auth required pam_deny.so` would then FAIL the whole stack even though pam_unix succeeded — that's exactly the lockout: correct password still denied.

So yes, removing pam_deny.so is the fix. And it should be inserted BEFORE pam_unix for biometric-first, or just appended as an additional factor with fail-open.

Let me keep it simple and correct: append only the bde-auth line with `success=1 default=ignore`, no pam_deny.

#!/bin/bash
# BDE HardLock Installer
# Enforces biometric authentication at boot and system lock.
#
# SAFETY: this edits /etc/pam.d for login, sudo, gdm-password, sshd and su.
# A mistake here locks you out of the machine, so:
#   - backups are taken and printed before anything is modified
#   - BDE_FAILMODE defaults to "open": if the biometric daemon is down,
#     authentication still succeeds on the normal password
#   - run with --dry-run first to see the exact commands
set -euo pipefail

DRY_RUN=0
[[ "${1:-}" == "--dry-run" ]] && DRY_RUN=1

# Services to hook. sshd is deliberately excluded unless asked for: it is the
# one that turns a bad PAM edit into a remote lockout with no console.
BDE_SERVICES=(login sudo gdm-password su)
[[ "${BDE_INCLUDE_SSHD:-0}" == "1" ]] && BDE_SERVICES+=(sshd)

run() {
    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
        echo "  [dry-run] $*"
    else
        "$@"
    fi
}

echo "=== BDE HardLock Installer ==="
echo "failmode : ${BDE_FAILMODE:-open} (daemon down => $([ "${BDE_FAILMODE:-open}" = open ] && echo 'auth still succeeds' || echo 'AUTH DENIED'))"
echo "services : ${BDE_SERVICES[*]}"
[ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ] && echo "mode     : DRY RUN, nothing will be modified"

# 0) Refuse to run as a non-dry-run if the verifier cannot be reached, because
#    a fail-open stack still needs a working daemon to be useful.
if [ "$DRY_RUN" != "1" ]; then
    if [ ! -x /usr/local/bin/bde-auth ]; then
        echo "[!] /usr/local/bin/bde-auth missing or not executable." >&2
        echo "    Install it first, or the PAM entry denies everything." >&2
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# 1) Install PAM biometrics stack
echo "[*] PAM biometrics packages..."
run sudo pacman -S --noconfirm --needed pam-biometric libfprint

# 2) Deploy BDE hardlock PAM config
echo "[*] Deploying bde-hardlock.pam..."
run sudo install -Dm644 /opt/bde/hardlock/bde-hardlock.pam /etc/pam.d/bde-hardlock

# 3) Hook into PAM stacks
echo "[*] Hooking PAM services..."
for service in "${BDE_SERVICES[@]}"; do
    [ -f "/etc/pam.d/$service" ] || continue
    if grep -q "bde-hardlock" "/etc/pam.d/$service" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "    $service: already hooked, skipping"
        continue
    fi
    echo "    $service: backing up"
    run sudo cp -a "/etc/pam.d/$service" "/etc/pam.d/$service.bde-backup.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)"
    # bde-auth returns 0 (skip the next line) only on a real biometric match.
    # On failure it returns non-zero, which `default=ignore` swallows, so the
    # normal password module still runs. There is deliberately NO pam_deny.so
    # here: that line turned every daemon hiccup into a locked-out session.
    run sudo sh -c "printf '%s\n' \
        'auth [success=1 default=ignore] /usr/local/bin/bde-auth' \
        >> /etc/pam.d/$service"
    echo "    $service: hooked"
done

# 4) Deploy systemd lock service
echo "[*] Installing bde-hardlock.service..."
run sudo install -Dm644 /opt/bde/hardlock/bde-hardlock.service /etc/systemd/system/bde-hardlock.service
run sudo systemctl daemon-reload
run sudo systemctl enable --now bde-hardlock.service

echo
if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[+] DRY RUN complete. Re-run without --dry-run to apply."
else
    echo "[+] BDE HardLock installed (failmode=${BDE_FAILMODE:-open})."
    echo "[*] Backups of every touched /etc/pam.d file are alongside it as *.bde-backup.*"
    echo "[*] To undo: restore those backups, then 'sudo systemctl disable --now bde-hardlock'."
fi

#!/bin/bash
# BDE HardLock Installer for BlackArch Linux
# Enforces biometric authentication at boot and system lock
set -euo pipefail

echo "=== BDE HardLock Patch for BlackArch ==="

# 1) Install PAM biometrics stack
echo "[*] Installing PAM biometrics..."
sudo pacman -S --noconfirm --needed pam-biometric libfprint 2>/dev/null || true

# 2) Deploy BDE hardlock PAM config
echo "[*] Deploying BDE hardlock PAM config..."
sudo install -Dm644 /opt/bde/hardlock/bde-hardlock.pam /etc/pam.d/bde-hardlock

# 3) Enable biometric authentication for login, sudo, gdm, ssh
echo "[*] Configuring system services..."
for service in login sudo gdm-password sshd su; do
  if [ -f "/etc/pam.d/$service" ]; then
    if ! grep -q "bde-hardlock" "/etc/pam.d/$service" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "auth [success=1 default=ignore] /usr/local/bin/bde-auth" | sudo tee -a "/etc/pam.d/$service" >/dev/null
      echo "auth required pam_deny.so" | sudo tee -a "/etc/pam.d/$service" >/dev/null
    fi
  fi
done

# 4) Deploy systemd lock service
echo "[*] Installing BDE lock service..."
sudo install -Dm644 /opt/bde/hardlock/bde-hardlock.service /etc/systemd/system/bde-hardlock.service
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now bde-hardlock.service

# 5) Deploy BlackArch-style package
echo "[*] Building BlackArch package..."
if command -v pacman >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -d /usr/share/blackarch ]; then
  sudo cp -r /opt/bde/blackarch/bde-hardlock /usr/share/blackarch/ 2>/dev/null || true
  sudo pacman -U --noconfirm /usr/share/blackarch/bde-hardlock/*.pkg.tar.zst 2>/dev/null || true
fi

echo "[+] BDE HardLock patch installed successfully"
echo "[*] Reboot to enforce biometric lock"
